voiceName: Hey Its Brad - Clear Narrator for Documentary

prompts.beat-01: [calmly] [slowly] Online safety is not about being afraid of your computer. [short pause] It is a set of small decisions you already know how to make. [short pause] You would not hand your house key to a stranger who knocked on the door, [short pause] and you would not sign a paper without reading it. [short pause] The same judgment works online. [short pause] Today you will set up your station so it is comfortable, spot a scam and check it a safer way, and protect your devices and files. [short pause] Then you will show five skills from this course and take the post-test. [short pause] Each step starts the same way. [short pause] Pause, look closely, and check before you act.
prompts.beat-02: [calmly] Start with your body and your screen. Sit so you can read without leaning in. The screen should be about an arm's length away, with the top near eye level. [short pause] If the words are too small, Magnifier makes everything bigger. Press the Windows key and plus to zoom in, and the Windows key and Escape to close it. [short pause] Browser zoom is different. It enlarges one website, and Control and zero puts it back. [short pause] Change one thing at a time, notice what got easier, and put shared settings back before you leave. If alerts keep pulling you away, Do not disturb quiets them while you work.
prompts.beat-03: [calmly] [slowly] Some features help far more people than you might expect. [short pause] Captions help in a noisy room, in a quiet library, and for anyone who hears less than they used to. [short pause] Keyboard access helps someone who cannot use a mouse. [short pause] Press Tab, and a visible outline moves from one control to the next. [short pause] Color is another one. [short pause] If a schedule shows full shifts only in dark shading, some people will miss it, and so will a black and white printer. [short pause] Put a word beside the color. [short pause] [encouraging] Mute this week's video, read its captions, and press Tab to watch the outline move. [short pause] Pause the video now.
prompts.beat-04: [calmly] Here is a fictional message. The subject says Act now: account will close. It comes from support at account-check dot example, and it asks you to verify your password immediately. [short pause] [serious] Three things should slow you down. The message pushes you to hurry. The sender does not match any organization you deal with. And it asks for a password, which a real organization will not request by email. [short pause] A familiar logo proves nothing, because anyone can copy a logo. Spelling can be perfect and the message can still be fake. [short pause] This kind of fake message is called phishing.
prompts.beat-05: [calmly] Never use the link or the phone number inside a suspicious message. Reach the organization another way. Open a bookmark you saved, type an address you know, or call the number on your card or letter. [short pause] Then ask whether the problem is real. [short pause] [reassuring] If you already typed your password, go to the real site, change it, and turn on two-step verification, so a code is needed as well. Then tell someone who can help. [short pause] [encouraging] Open the Mission 5B practice page. Inspect the subject, the sender, and the link, and write two warning signs and your safer check. [short pause] Pause the video now.
prompts.beat-06: [calmly] Not every risk arrives as an email. A new online friend may be warm and patient for weeks, then ask for money, often gift cards, and ask you to keep it secret. [short pause] Secrecy and money together are a reason to stop and check with someone you trust. [short pause] Scrolling late at night because you might miss something is a real pull too. Set a stopping point, or quiet your alerts. [short pause] [reassuring] If someone posts something hurtful about you, do not reply in anger. Keep a screenshot if it is safe, report or block, and talk to someone. [short pause] [encouraging] Write a safe next step for each situation on your worksheet. [short pause] Pause the video now.
prompts.beat-07: [calmly] Updates fix security holes, so let Windows Update do its job. [short pause] Home computers still on Windows 10 need Extended Security Updates, which run through October 2027, or a move to a supported device. [short pause] A website may ask to use your camera or microphone. Allow it when the task needs it, such as a video meeting, and block it when it does not, such as a page you only read. A permission can stay on after a call ends, so check it in your browser settings now and then. [short pause] If you find a USB drive you do not recognize, do not plug it in. Give it to staff.
prompts.beat-08: [calmly] Different protections do different jobs. In Word, a password to open a file encrypts it, so nobody can read it without that password. [short pause] Read-only only limits changes; anyone can still read the words. Device encryption protects a laptop that is lost while turned off. [short pause] None of these protect a computer left signed in, so press Windows and L to lock it, or sign out of a shared computer. [short pause] For accounts, use a passkey when a site offers one. Otherwise use a long, unique passphrase with two-step verification. [short pause] [encouraging] On the Mission 5C practice page, choose before you flip each card, then look at the settings your worksheet names. [short pause] Pause the video now.
prompts.beat-09: [calmly] [slowly] Now you get to show what you can do. [short pause] The skills challenge has five tasks, and you work on your own. [short pause] Ask a search question that names the place, and open the organization's own page. [short pause] Build a short Word paragraph with a real heading, three numbered steps, and a bold warning. [short pause] Total four costs in Excel with a formula. [short pause] Delete a line, then bring it back with Undo. [short pause] And write useful feedback on a partner's flyer. [short pause] The quick card is allowed. [short pause] Your instructor watches and records how much help you needed. [short pause] [reassuring] This is separate from your test score, and it shows what you can already do on your own.
prompts.beat-10: [calmly] [slowly] Last comes the post-test. [short pause] It has twenty questions, and you take it on your own, with no coaching. [short pause] When you finish, submit your results to Britt and save the complete graded PDF. [short pause] The results show your score and which areas went well. [short pause] [warmly] Treat them as a learning plan, not a verdict. [short pause] Pick one strength to keep using and one skill to practice next. [short pause] Then compare where you started on the pre-test with where you are now. [short pause] Every row you completed in this course is something you can do again at home, at your own pace.
